mechanism.verified_finding_honored: KernelRunStore.lease_next_wake is a NON-ATOMIC, lock-free read-modify-write. The ONLY thing that prevents two drainers double-leasing the same wake is the SERVICE-LAYER fcntl.flock in run_kernel_daemon_service (LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on <store>/daemon_service.lock — one shared lock path per store). A control experiment proved two drainers on SEPARATE lock paths against the same store DOUBLE-LEASE.
mechanism.enqueue_side: On the SHARED store the agent's governed wake is ENQUEUE-ONLY. _govern_wake_via_kernel calls kernel.enqueue_source_wake('persistent_self_wake', payload, wake_id=f'persistent_self_wake:{self.name}:{correlation_id}') and returns {run_id, status='queued', wake_id, shared=True} WITHOUT leasing or running. enqueue_source_wake -> enqueue_wake -> _append_wake_record is append-only (status=queued). The deterministic agent-scoped wake_id prevents cross-agent collision in the shared ledger. The per-agent (unset env) default keeps the inline kernel.wake() drain.
mechanism.spawn_side: Agent A additionally spawns a subagent-wake into the shared store via kernel.spawn_subagent_wake(parent_envelope, child_agent_uid, task_text, allowed_files=<subset of parent>, requested_tools=['session_status'], tool_calls=[...], wake_id=...). spawn_subagent_wake is also enqueue-only (status 'spawned') — the explicit parent/child coordination primitive; the child inherits A's parent_run_id and a subset of A's authority.
mechanism.drain_side: A SINGLE run_kernel_daemon_service(store_dir=<shared>, ..., cycles=N, max_wakes=M, interval_seconds=0) drains the shared store. Its lock defaults to <store>/daemon_service.lock — ONE shared lock path — acquired NON-BLOCKING via fcntl.flock. Inside the lock it runs run_daemon_cycle -> run_control_tick -> run_next_wake (lease_next_wake + run + complete_wake) + closeback_source_wake. Because every drain goes through this ONE flock on ONE lock path, lease_next_wake's non-atomicity is serialized -> EXACTLY-ONCE lease + exactly-once terminal.
mechanism.workspace_root_stays_per_agent: workspace_root=self.state_dir is kept per-agent, so each agent's witness/closeback roots are unchanged; ONLY the kernel ledgers are shared.
mechanism.load_bearing_rule: Never two concurrent direct lease_next_wake on a shared store off separate locks. The agents NEVER lease on the shared store (enqueue-only); leasing happens solely inside the single flock-held daemon service. A's own task still ran first in step 8 (observe+govern never replaces the agent's work).

how_to_enable: Coordination is OFF by default and requires BOTH env vars set on the process(es) that run your persistent agents.

1. Choose a shared directory both agents can reach on the same machine (the kernel's lease atomicity is single-host / local-FS — the daemon flock is a local fcntl lock). E.g. `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_STORE_DIR=/Users/dhyana/.dharma/shared_kernel`. Both agents will root their governed-wake KernelRunStore at <that dir>/living_agent_kernel.

2. Turn governance on for both agents: `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE=1`. With BOTH vars set, each agent's wake ENQUEUES its governed wake into the shared store (it does NOT inline-drain — that is the safety property).

3. Run a SINGLE kernel daemon service to drain the shared store. The ONLY safe drainer is run_kernel_daemon_service pointed at <shared>/living_agent_kernel; its flock (<shared>/daemon_service.lock) serializes all draining so each queued wake is leased and governed EXACTLY ONCE. Do NOT run two un-coordinated drainers on separate lock paths, and do NOT have the agents inline-drain a shared store — either re-introduces the proven double-lease.

4. To revert to per-agent (non-shared) governance: `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_STORE_DIR` (keep or drop the governance flag as desired). Each agent then roots its store under its own state_dir and inline-completes exactly as before — byte-identical. To turn off all governance: `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE`.

NOTE: this build proves the mechanism in an isolated worktree with a stubbed LLM step (no provider/network). The shared dir and both env vars are test-/operator-set ONLY — they are NOT added to any launchd plist or live .env. Before trusting it in production: (a) carry the kernel seam modules into the worktree that runs your live daemon (they exist only in lak-e2e — flag-on silently no-ops without them), and (b) run one live-provider flag-on smoke under approved budget.

learning_loop.unit: CLOSE THE LEARNING LOOP (lessons read-back) — when enabled, a governed wake READS this agent's OWN accumulated lessons (by agent_uid) back from the durable hash-chained KernelLessonStore ledger and INJECTS a compact 'Prior lessons:' preamble into the ReAct INPUT before the agent runs its task, so the agent's next action is informed by what it previously learned. The existing write/govern path (step 8b) then appends new lessons. The loop closes: wake N writes lesson L (existing LEARN executor) -> wake N+1 reads L back into its context.

ReAct input == task_text byte-for-byte. Proven by test_flag_off_is_byte_identical_no_readback.
flag.how_to_enable: BOTH env vars must be set on the process that runs the persistent-agent daemon: `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE=1` AND `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_LESSONS_READBACK=1`. With both set, each wake reads this agent's own accumulated lessons (agent:{name}:lessons) and prepends a 'Prior lessons:' preamble to the ReAct input. To disable read-back only: `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_LESSONS_READBACK` (governance/receipts continue). To disable everything: also `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE`.

read_back_mechanism.read_accessor: KernelLessonStore.recent_valid_lessons(namespace, *, limit=5) — re-derives each row's entry_hash (the identical per-row check verify_lesson_ledger uses: blank entry_hash -> stable_payload_hash(material)) and SKIPS any row whose hash no longer verifies OR that fails Pydantic validation, returning up to `limit` most-recent SURVIVING receipts in ledger order. Never raises: a missing/empty ledger yields []. This is the tamper-safe read primitive — a forged/corrupted row is never returned, so it cannot be injected into the agent's context.
read_back_mechanism.namespace_alignment: Read namespace = f'agent:{self.name}:lessons' (persistent_agent.py:529). This is EXACTLY the namespace the LEARN executor writes to: f'agent:{agent_uid}:lessons' (living_agent_kernel.py), with agent_uid == PersistentAgent.name (persistent_adapter.py). Write and read therefore target the identical file.
read_back_mechanism.store_root_alignment: The read roots a KernelLessonStore at _persistent_kernel_store_dir(self.state_dir) — the SAME base_dir the governed-wake write path uses (per-agent by default, or the shared store when DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_STORE_DIR is set). The read sees exactly what the write produced.
read_back_mechanism.injection_point: persistent_agent.py wake() step 7b, immediately BEFORE step 8's `agent_result = await self._agent.wake(react_input)`. Mechanism: `react_input = task_text` unconditionally (so flag-off is byte-identical); if _persistent_kernel_lessons_readback_enabled() then preamble = self._read_back_lessons_preamble() and, only when non-empty, `react_input = f'{preamble}\n\n{task_text}'` plus result_info['lessons_injected']=True. Step 8 then calls self._agent.wake(react_input).
read_back_mechanism.governance_witness_unchanged: CRITICAL: the original task_text is preserved and is what step 8b governance (_govern_wake_via_kernel(task_text)) and the witness log still receive. Only the ReAct INPUT is augmented — the governance/receipt/audit path is byte-identical to the governance-only unit. Verified by reviewer #2: governance got 'TASKONLY' while react_input carried the augmented 'PRIOR LESSON' text.
read_back_mechanism.preamble_shape: Best-effort _read_back_lessons_preamble(self, *, limit=5): try-imports KernelLessonStore, reads recent_valid_lessons, builds 'Prior lessons:\n- ...\n- ...' where each lesson's delta_text is whitespace-collapsed and capped at 300 chars. Returns '' on any Exception (logged at debug). Bounded: limit=5 x 300 chars => ~1KB worst case (~944 bytes measured on a 5000-row ledger).
read_back_mechanism.best_effort: Reading lessons is wrapped so ANY failure (no ledger, empty, tamper, read error, forced exception) -> the agent proceeds with its NORMAL task and NO injected lessons. Read-back can NEVER block or break the wake. The accessor itself never raises on a malformed ledger, and the helper has an outer try/except returning ''.

how_to_enable: Read-back is OFF by default and requires BOTH env vars set on the process that runs the persistent-agent daemon.
1. Governance must be on first (read-back is a strict subset): `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE=1`.

2. Turn read-back on: `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_LESSONS_READBACK=1` (truthy = 1/true/yes/on; anything else = OFF). With BOTH set, each wake reads this agent's OWN accumulated lessons (agent:{name}:lessons) from the durable hash-chained ledger and prepends a compact 'Prior lessons:' preamble (last 5 valid lessons, each capped 300 chars) to the ReAct INPUT before the agent runs. The original task_text drives governance/witness unchanged.

3. To disable read-back only (keep governance + receipts): `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_LESSONS_READBACK`. To disable everything: also `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE`. Either revert is byte-identical to current behavior.

NOTE: like the governance + coordination units, this is proven in the isolated lak-e2e worktree with a STUBBED LLM step (no provider/network). Before trusting it in production: (a) carry the kernel seam modules into the live-daemon worktree (they exist only in lak-e2e — flag-on silently no-ops without them), and (b) to claim BEHAVIORAL improvement (not just read-back-into-context), run one live-provider flag-on smoke under approved budget showing the answer changes with vs without the preamble — that demo was NOT run here and the behavioral claim is NOT made.
